title: Cross-Product Cutover Concierge: automated notifications, escalation SLAs & runbook tagging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a lightweight "cutover concierge" layer that standardizes notifications, escalation SLAs, and runbook tagging for cross-product releases (runtime / console / API). This ticket scopes the PM playbook, required automation hooks, and a minimal set of runbook metadata tags to support oncall triage, regional blackout handling, and fast rollback decisions. The concierge is not a new service — it's a set of templates, event mappings, and notification rules baked into the release pipeline and Console alerting UI. Expected outcome: reduced cutover decision time, consistent owner handoffs, and fewer ad-hoc Slack escalations during launch windows.
acceptance_criteria: Notification templates defined for canary, ramp, and full-cutover phases and published in Confluence
Automated notification flow implemented for Canary -> Ramp -> Full with configurable SLAs (acknowledge: 15m, respond: 30m)
Runbook tagging taxonomy agreed and applied to 3 pilot runbooks (runtime KV cache changes, console feature flag rollout, API quota change)
Escalation path wired into PagerDuty with a documented 3-step SLA and fallback owner list
Cutover concierge checklist integrated with Launch Calendar dashboard and visible in Console release row
tasks: Draft Confluence playbook: notification templates, escalation matrix, runbook tagging taxonomy
Add webhook mapping in CI pipeline to emit cutover-phase events to Notifications service (ENG task)
Create PagerDuty escalation policy and test with oncall rota
Tag pilot runbooks and run two dry-run cutovers in staging
Update Launch Calendar UI to surface acknowledge/respond buttons and SLA state
updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with Eng, SRE, Console, and Runtime teams — aligned on scope and pilot cutovers (runtime KV cache change, console rollout).
2026-03-11: Eng spike completed — webhook mapping requires a small protobuf schema change (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4572). Marcos (ENG) estimates 3 dev days.
2026-03-12: PM review with Legal and Security — no additional controls required for notification content; security confirmed no sensitive data should be in notifications.
2026-03-12: Updated acceptance criteria to include tagging taxonomy and Launch Calendar integration after feedback from Console PMs.
risks: Runbook tagging adoption may be slow across teams — mitigation: require tags for all production-cutover PRs during pilot
PagerDuty policy churn could create noisy escalations — mitigation: limited rollout and testing in staging for two cycles
Over-automation risk where notifications obscure human judgement — mitigation: checklist includes explicit human decision gates
Cross-region cutovers may need region-specific blackout logic beyond initial scope
decisions: Use existing Notifications service and extend event schema rather than building a new notifier
SLA windows set to acknowledge=15m, respond=30m for pilot (adjustable after two live launches)
Pilot includes three runbooks representing runtime, console, and API surfaces
Runbook tags will use a small controlled vocabulary: phase, owner-role, rollback-trigger, obs-links
